results.description:
The EB\-MIND (Engineering Biology for Metal Recovery from Industrial Waste Streams) project aims to pioneer a novel approach for the biorecovery of platinum group metals (PGMs) from industrial effluents using advanced engineering biology techniques. This multidisciplinary project brings together experts from geomicrobiology, molecular biology, material science, catalysis, and life cycle assessment to develop scalable and sustainable biotechnologies for metal recovery.


We are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join our team and lead the environmental impact and circularity assessment work package (WP4\). This role will involve applying life cycle assessment (LCA) tools and developing a circular economy framework to evaluate the environmental sustainability and circularity of the EB\-MIND processes. The successful candidate will work closely with industrial partners, including Johnson Matthey, to compare the environmental impacts of engineered biological processes against existing industrial practices.


The post\-holder will be based within an interdisciplinary and collegiate team of researchers at the Tyndall Centre for Climate Change Research at the Department of Civil Engineering and Management (University of Manchester). We are looking for a person with a passion for research and a demonstrable skill to work in a highly interdisciplinary environment. Aligned with the Tyndall Centre’s missions, you will contribute towards the research team’s efforts to conduct research with genuine impact on policy and practice, and to publish in the very highest quality journals (indicatively, these might be Nature Sustainability, Journal of Cleaner Production and Resource Conservation and Recycling). Flexible working arrangements will be considered.


More detailed information about the responsibilities of the post and selection criteria can be found in the ‘Further Particulars’ document attached at the bottom of this advert.

results.title: Research Associate – Molecular Mechanisms Driving Liver Cancer Development
results.description:
We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join Professor Karen Piper Hanley’s team to investigate how mechanical and microenvironmental changes reshape liver cell behaviour during chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression.


This project will combine advanced liver organoid systems, mouse models, and translational human liver disease cohorts to uncover how extracellular matrix remodelling, tissue stiffness, and inflammatory microenvironments drive cellular plasticity and malignant transformation. A major focus will be understanding how mechanical stress alters nuclear membrane responses, transcriptional regulation, and intercellular communication during disease progression.


The successful candidate will develop and apply mechanistic wet\-lab approaches alongside cutting\-edge single\-cell and spatial technologies, including spatial transcriptomics and emerging cellcell interaction methodologies. The project offers opportunities to integrate advanced imaging, functional genomics, organoid biology, and translational tissue analysis within a highly interdisciplinary research environment.


The laboratory is embedded within the Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health at The University of Manchester and has strong links with the Manchester Cell\-Matrix Centre, an internationally recognised centre focused on mechanobiology, extracellular matrix biology, fibrosis, and tissue remodelling. The postholder will benefit from access to outstanding genomics, imaging, spatial transcriptomics, and computational infrastructure, as well as close interactions with researchers across hepatology, developmental biology, cancer and matrix biology.


The successful candidate will take a leading role in driving this research programme, including planning and performing experiments, developing new experimental systems, integrating multi\-modal datasets, and producing high\-quality work for publication. The postholder will also contribute actively to collaborative projects, supervision of junior researchers, and the development of future research directions and grant applications within the laboratory.


Applicants should hold (or be close to completing) a PhD in an area of molecular \& cell biology, or a related discipline. The ability to demonstrate excellent communication skills, a collaborative mindset, and enthusiasm for contributing to a vibrant research environment are essential.

results.title: Research Associate in X-ray Imaging of Cementitious Materials – X-SeeO2
results.description:
Partnering with the University of Bath, the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF), France, and led by Miguel Ángel García, Professor of Inorganic Chemistry at the University of Malaga (UMA), we have formed a consortium, X\-SeeO2, that has been selected by the EIC under the Pathfinder “Cement as Carbon Sinks" Challenge call to receive 4 million in funding. The Challenge seeks to support breakthrough innovations and (alternative) pathways for decarbonized and carbon\-negative cement and concrete while maintaining its structural integrity and durability. This is important because cement and concrete technologies contribute around 8% of our CO2 emissions (about 600 kg per capita), which are “embodied” in our buildings and infrastructures.


Our 'X\-SeeO2' project has been selected as a key 'enabling technology'. This means that the micro\-computed tomography (microCT) analysis methods that will be pioneered within the National X\-ray Computed Tomography facility (NXCT) located in the Royce Institute at Manchester and at the ESRF will be used to accelerate and improve the products and technologies arising out of the other innovation projects that have been selected within this same pathfinder challenge in this latest EIC Horizon Europe call. These methods will reveal the 3D structure and evolution of microstructure of concrete non\-destructively and make these methods available to other researchers across the “Cement as Carbon Sinks" Challenge.


The successful candidate will help to develop protocols for imaging, characterizing and quantifying the various cement phases as well as the porosity (volume fraction, pore size, connectivity etc) using lab. And synchrotron X\-ray CT as well as developing new characterization modalities. In addition the researcher will liaise with, and support, the time resolved characterisation of low carbon cements of other teams within the Pathfinder challenge. They will be based in Manchester but also make trips to the ESRF in Grenoble as well as to our collaborators in Malaga and Bath. Others within the group will develop in situ rigs for studying the kinetics of the hydration and carbonation reactions (ex\-situ and in\-situ) by laboratory and synchrotron powder diffraction (for crystalline component time\-evolution) and laboratory and synchrotron computer tomography (for microstructure time\-evolution, including carbonate\-shrinkage). The diffraction studies will be carried out by other X\-SeeO2 staff.

**Purpose of the Job**


The successful candidate will carry out X\-ray imaging/tomographic research on cementitious materials, with the focus being the carbonation processes. The team at the ESRF will develop an in\-situ carbonation cell under moderate CO2 pressures. The researcher will undertake time resolved and ex\-situ studies of cementitious materials within the Henry Moseley X\-ray Imaging Facility (which leads the National Facility for Lab. X\-ray CT (nxct.ac.uk)) in Manchester, which is one of the most extensive suites of CT scanners in Europe. They will also undertake and support some experiments at the ESRF.


The post holder will be located at the University of Manchester but will be expected to carry out some experiments at the ESRF and to travel to the collaborators to attend meetings.

results.description:
Founded in 2012, LADbible Group is redefining entertainment and news for a social generation. Our global community engages with our content–spanning editorial, video, documentary and live – we reach 1 billion people each and every month. Our mission is to give the youth generation a voice by building communities that laugh, think and act. Using all major platforms, we’ve rapidly risen to become one of the world's largest publishers.


3 days in our Manchester office, 2 days working from home


As a Editorial Researcher / Social Editor for LADbible, you will be responsible for delivering trending and breaking news to our vast audience 24/7…You will know what they want to hear, how they want to hear it, and when they want to hear it; building a daily schedule based on what news is happening that day, what original stories we are using and what stories our readers engage with most using data\-informed decision\-making.


You will be responsible for packaging, posting and measuring the success of articles and using that knowledge to continually improve and target wider audiences.


Sitting as a key member of our team at LADbible Group, this role is vital in the performance of our site and offers some excellent learning and progression opportunities.

**What the opportunity looks like:**

* Proactively research and seek the latest videos, news, trends, gossip and reports ahead of other major brands
* Have the ability to instinctively spot a story that the audience will love to watch or hear about, with a focus on original storytelling
* Develop an understanding of our core audience and demonstrate awareness of audience topics and trends
* Having a 360\-degree approach to sourcing content, taking into account the various ways in which audiences can reach our content via different mediums
* Collaborate on ideas with other social editors and writers within the team, working together to develop concepts for audience and make them better
* Scheduling and posting content via Facebook, Twitter and Instagram
* Packaging articles \- creating captions, titles and thumbnails to help generate traffic
* Regularly monitor insights using social media analysis tools and review and report on effectiveness to maximise results
* Adopting other methods of growing audience from other referrers, including search
* Use initiative and creativity to bring new ideas to the team, sharing knowledge and contributing to ongoing improvements
* Working across a seven\-day rota and covering live events as they happen

**Skills and experience we’d like you to have:**

* Experience in social media, with a strong knowledge of Facebook, Instagram and Twitter a necessity.
* A strong interest in the UK news cycle, pop culture and viral content for a youth audience.
* A university degree and/or equivalent to Journalism / Broadcasting / Media
* Demonstrated a clear knowledge and passion for trending news and how to produce original stories
* Worked as part of a team and been able to demonstrate strong teamwork skills as part of that
* Have clear examples of social campaigns worked on and/or a portfolio of social posts or articles that have helped deliver audience
* An understanding or willingness to understand search engine optimisation
* Have held some responsibility for selection of content for a digital audience
* Knowledge of journalism law and ethics

Overview:

Principal Mechanical Design Engineer – Shape the Future of Scientific Discovery


Waters Wilmslow is looking for a Principal Mechanical Design Engineer to become a key technical leader within our Mechanical Engineering team, the group behind the mechanical innovation powering our global Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer product range.


This is a role for someone who wants to own architecture‑level decisions, guide engineering direction, and influence the next generation of world‑leading analytical instruments. You’ll work at the intersection of precision engineering, scientific discovery, and advanced manufacturing, helping to define platforms that will be used by researchers and scientists across the world.


If you’re motivated by solving complex mechanical challenges, mentoring talented engineers, and shaping technology strategy at scale, this is a rare opportunity to make a lasting impact.


Responsibilities:
**What You’ll Lead \& Influence**


Technical Authority \& Architecture

* Act as the go‑to technical authority for mechanical design across the Quan Portfolio and own key mechanical architectures and drive critical design decisions.
* Lead the development of high‑precision mechanical systems, including electro‑mechanical assemblies and vacuum technologies.
* Apply Design for Excellence (DfX) to optimise performance, manufacturability, cost, and risk.

  

Project Leadership Across the Full Lifecycle

* Guide mechanical design from concept through new product introduction, release, and continuous improvement.
* Translate cross‑functional requirements into robust, high‑quality product solutions.
* Contribute to long‑term platform strategy, technology roadmaps, and engineering capability development.

  

Team Development \& Engineering Excellence

* Mentor and develop engineers, strengthening technical judgement and professional growth.
* Set and uphold engineering standards, best practices, and quality expectations.
* Peer review drawings, documentation, and change requests to ensure technical consistency and excellence.

  

Cross‑Functional Collaboration \& Supplier Engagement

* Work closely with electronics, development scientists, production, product assurance, and supply chain teams to deliver integrated solutions.
* Partner with suppliers to develop cost‑effective manufacturing approaches and explore emerging techniques.

  

Continuous Improvement \& Compliance

* Diagnose and resolve complex mechanical issues across the Quan Portfolio.
* Produce high‑quality technical documentation aligned with Waters Quality Standards.
* Stay current with advances in mechanical engineering and scientific instrumentation — and bring that innovation into our products.
* Represent Waters at exhibitions, seminars, and training events when required.


Qualifications:
**What You Bring**

* Degree in Mechanical Engineering (or related discipline) or equivalent industry experience.
* Extensive experience designing precision mechanical systems using 3D CAD (SolidWorks or Siemens NX).
* Strong capability in 2D drawings and GD\&T.
* Proven experience with complex electro‑mechanical assemblies, vacuum systems, and thermally sensitive designs.
* A track record of leading mechanical design through the full product lifecycle.
* Demonstrated technical leadership and ownership of major design decisions.
* Experience working within a recognised quality management system.

 **Why Join Waters?**


At Waters, you’ll work in an environment where technical excellence, collaboration, and innovation are genuinely valued. You’ll help shape world‑leading analytical instruments while continuing to grow your own technical and leadership capabilities at a senior level.

**You’ll also receive**:

* Competitive salary and benefits
* Above‑average holiday allowance
* Strong pension contributions
* Career development within a global life science leader

  

We’re committed to building diverse, inclusive teams where everyone can contribute their best work. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and can make reasonable adjustments throughout the interview process.

We collaborate with customers around the world to advance the release of effective, high\-quality medicines, ensure the safety of food and water, and drive better patient outcomes by detecting diseases earlier, managing routine infections, and combating antibiotic resistance.
